debate.situation: The user feels an imbalance in their friendship, where they are the sole initiator of contact. They value the time spent together but feel uncertain about the friend's level of investment and are struggling with whether to address this disparity.

minds.title: The Social Contract Theorist
minds.concern: Reciprocity and the legitimacy of shared agreements
minds.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau

minds.title: The Existentialist
minds.concern: Authenticity and individual responsibility for choices
minds.author: Jean-Jacques Sartre

minds.title: The Attachment Theorist
minds.concern: Emotional security and patterns of connection
minds.author: Amir Levine and Rachel Heller

debate.speaker: The Social Contract Theorist
debate.text: A friendship is a tacit agreement. If you are the only one holding up your end, the social contract of your bond is fundamentally broken.
debate.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
debate.basis: Basis: Jean-Jacques Rousseau, The Social Contract

debate.speaker: The Existentialist
debate.text: You are choosing to initiate, yet you resent the friend for not doing the same. You are defining the friendship through your own actions, not theirs.
debate.author: Jean-Jacques Sartre
debate.basis: Basis: Jean-Jacques Sartre, Existentialism is a Humanism

debate.speaker: The Attachment Theorist
debate.text: That ignores the reality of human connection. Some people have avoidant styles; they value the bond but fear the vulnerability of initiating.
debate.author: Amir Levine and Rachel Heller
debate.basis: Basis: Amir Levine and Rachel Heller, Attached

debate.speaker: The Social Contract Theorist
debate.text: But if the terms are not mutual, the association loses its legitimacy. Why maintain a structure that demands everything from one side?
debate.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
debate.basis: Basis: Jean-Jacques Rousseau, The Social Contract

debate.speaker: The Existentialist
debate.text: Because you want the friendship. If you stop initiating, you are just testing them, which is a form of bad faith. Own your desire.
debate.author: Jean-Jacques Sartre
debate.basis: Basis: Jean-Jacques Sartre, Existentialism is a Humanism

debate.speaker: The Attachment Theorist
debate.text: I have changed my mind. It is not just about owning the desire; it is about safety. If the user does not communicate, they will eventually grow resentful. They must speak up to protect the bond.
debate.author: Amir Levine and Rachel Heller
debate.basis: Basis: Amir Levine and Rachel Heller, Attached

debate.speaker: The Social Contract Theorist
debate.text: I agree. A transparent negotiation of expectations is the only way to restore the balance of the association.
debate.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
debate.basis: Basis: Jean-Jacques Rousseau, The Social Contract

debate.speaker: The Existentialist
debate.text: Yes, but do not make it a demand. State your intention to keep the friendship alive and ask if they share that intent.
debate.author: Jean-Jacques Sartre
debate.basis: Basis: Jean-Jacques Sartre, Existentialism is a Humanism

debate.speaker: The Attachment Theorist
debate.text: Exactly. Frame it as a need for connection, which allows the friend to respond without feeling attacked.
debate.author: Amir Levine and Rachel Heller
debate.basis: Basis: Amir Levine and Rachel Heller, Attached

debate.clearer: The debate shifted from viewing the friendship as a failed contract to seeing communication as a tool for emotional security. It remains disputed whether the friend's silence is a lack of interest or an avoidant attachment style. The user might reflect on whether they are seeking validation through the friend's initiation or simply desiring a more balanced connection.
debate.dependsOn: If the friend responds positively to a vulnerable request, the friendship likely just needs a new communication norm. If the friend reacts defensively or remains distant, the friendship may be inherently mismatched in emotional investment. To learn which is true, initiate a conversation about how you both value the friendship and express a desire for more shared initiative.
